mainTopic: Handle questions that end in תיקו, the טומאה of אבר מן החי and flesh from a living animal, and flesh cut from such a limb
overview: This עמוד opens by finishing a series of 'handle' questions. Can a part that cannot itself become טמא pass טומאה to the part attached to it, the way a יד does? The question is asked about a half-worshipped gourd, a fig branch hanging by its bark (רב פפא), and a corner stone shared by two houses with a נגע (רבי זירא), and all three end in תיקו. The גמרא then returns to the משנה and explains how אבר מן החי differs from אבר מן הנבלה: flesh that comes off the first is טהור, but flesh that comes off the second is טמא. רב learns the טומאה of אבר מן החי from 'וכי ימות מן הבהמה', and the extra wording of the פסוק also teaches that a slaughtered טרפה is not טמא as a נבלה. A ברייתא explains why flesh from a living animal is not טמא, with three tests: it grows back (רבי יוסי הגלילי), it lacks sinews and bones (רבי עקיבא), or it lacks flesh, sinews and bones together (רבי). The same three views appear for שרצים, and the גמרא explains why both teachings are needed. Finally, a ברייתא rules that flesh cut from an אבר מן החי is טמא only if it was set aside as food before it was cut. רבי אסי begins to question that ruling, and his question continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Can the forbidden half of the gourd be a handle for the other half?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the half of the gourd that cannot become טמא can still act as a יד and carry טומאה to the other half.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law: does it become a handle for its partner?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the earlier case of a gourd that was half worshipped as עבודה זרה. It asks whether the forbidden half, which cannot become טמא itself, can pass טומאה to the permitted half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, the forbidden half is not treated as food, so it cannot become טמא as food. Normally, a יד (handle) passes טומאה to the food attached to it even though the handle itself is not food. The question is whether this non-food half acts like a handle for the other half.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the law? (opens a question)
A handle: an attached part that passes טומאה to the food it holds
Its partner, meaning the other half of the gourd

steps.confusionAlert: The forbidden half is still a real part of the gourd. The question is only whether it can carry טומאה over to the permitted half, even though it cannot become טמא as food on its own.

phrases.english: What is the law: does it become a handle for its partner?
phrases.notes: A handle passes טומאה along: if the handle touches something טמא, the food attached to it becomes טמא too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the gourd discussion from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a part that cannot become טמא as food can act as a יד and pass טומאה to the attached part that can.

steps.title: The gourd question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The question about the gourd is left open with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot find an answer, so it leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means the question 'stands' without a decision. No proof was found either way about whether the forbidden half acts as a handle.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question stays unresolved
A dilemma, a question with no clear answer yet

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 1 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It is undecided whether the non-טמא half of the gourd serves as a יד for the other half.

steps.title: רב פפא quotes the case of a fig branch mostly torn off
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא quotes a משנה about a fig branch hanging by its bark. רבי יהודה says the fruit cannot become טמא. חכמים say it depends on whether the branch can live.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: They taught: A fig branch that was torn off but is still attached by its bark: רבי יהודה rules it טהור. חכמים say: if it can live, it is טהור; if not, it is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a משנה about a fig branch that is mostly broken off the tree. He is setting up a new question in the same style as the gourd question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fruit still attached to a tree cannot become טמא. A branch hanging only by its bark is a borderline case. רבי יהודה treats it as still attached, so it is always טהור. חכמים say it counts as attached only if it could reattach and keep growing; otherwise it is like picked fruit and can become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A branch or shoot
Was split or torn off
Still attached, connected
Bark or peel
Rules it טהור, here meaning it cannot become טמא
Able to live, meaning it could heal and keep growing

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'טהור' does not mean the fruit was cleaned of טומאה. It means the fruit cannot become טמא at all, because it still counts as attached to the tree.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Behold, they said
phrases.notes: He is quoting a משנה in עוקצין 3:8.

phrases.english: a branch of a fig tree that was torn off
and is still attached by its bark –
Rabbi Yehuda rules it pure,
and the Sages say:
if it is able to live – it is pure,
and if not – it is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel case to set up a dilemma like the gourd question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fig branch hanging by its bark: רבי יהודה says it cannot become טמא; חכמים say it cannot become טמא only if it could reattach and live.

steps.title: Can the living branch be a handle for the branch attached to it?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whether a branch that cannot become טמא acts as a handle for a second branch growing from it that can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: What is the law: does it become a handle for its fellow?
steps.whatsHappening: Using the חכמים's view, רב פפא asks the same handle question about the fig branches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture one branch that could still live, so it cannot become טמא, and a second branch growing out of it that could not live, so it can become טמא. If the first branch touches טומאה, does it pass the טומאה on to the second branch like a handle?

keyTerms.meaning: Its fellow, meaning the second branch attached to it

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
What is the law: does it become a handle for its fellow?
phrases.notes: 'Its fellow' is a second branch growing from this one that could not live, so that branch can become טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא: מַהוּ שֶׁיֵּעָשֶׂה יָד לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a handle question on top of the משנה quoted in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a branch that cannot become טמא can pass טומאה as a יד to an attached branch that can.

steps.title: The fig branch question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא's question also ends with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: Again the גמרא cannot decide, so the question is left open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the gourd case, the גמרא finds no proof about whether a part that cannot become טמא can serve as a handle. Both dilemmas remain open.
steps.whatToRemember: Two cases in a row, the gourd and the fig branch, raise the same question: can a part that cannot become טמא pass טומאה along like a handle? Both end in תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב פפא's question without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It is undecided whether the living branch serves as a יד for the branch attached to it.

steps.title: רבי זירא quotes the case of a corner stone shared by two houses
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes a משנה about a corner stone shared by two houses. When it is pulled out for a נגע, the whole stone is removed. When the house is torn down, only his part is destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: They taught: A stone in the corner: when he pulls it out, he pulls out all of it; when he tears down, he tears down his own part and leaves his neighbor's part.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא brings a משנה about a house with a נגע (צרעת mark) on a corner stone shared with a neighbor. He is setting up another dilemma in this series, which will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A corner stone can belong to two houses at once. If a נגע appears on it, the stone must be pulled out, and the whole stone goes, even the neighbor's side. If the house later has to be torn down, only the owner's part of the stone is destroyed and the neighbor's part stays.

keyTerms.meaning: A corner stone, part of the walls of two houses
Pulls out a stone that has a נגע
Tears down the whole house
Leaves in place

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up חוֹלֵץ and נוֹתֵץ. חוֹלֵץ means taking out the affected stone, and then the whole stone goes. נוֹתֵץ means destroying the house, and then only his own part of the stone goes.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: Behold, they said:
phrases.notes: He is quoting a משנה in נגעים 13:2.

phrases.english: a stone that is in the corner,
when he pulls it out – he pulls out all of it,
and when he tears down – he tears down his own part
and leaves that of his neighbor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a third parallel case, setting up a new dilemma after the two תיקו questions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a shared corner stone with a נגע: when pulling it out, the whole stone is removed; when tearing down the house, only the owner's part is destroyed and the neighbor's part is left.

steps.title: Can one half of the shared stone be a handle for the other half?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks whether the half of the corner stone in the neighbor's house counts as a יד (handle) for the half in the house with the נגע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asks: what is the law? Does one half of the stone become a handle for the other half?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא builds on the משנה about a corner stone shared by two houses, which he quoted in step 6. He asks whether one half of the stone counts as a 'handle' for the other half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In other areas of טומאה, a handle attached to food is treated as part of it, so touching the handle can pass on the טומאה. רבי זירא asks whether this rule of יד also works for a house with a נגע. If it does, the neighbor's half of the stone would be linked to the טמא half.

keyTerms.meaning: A handle; an attached part that is treated as joined to the main item for טומאה
For its fellow; here, the other half of the same stone
A צרעת mark, here on the stones of a house
He asks; a real question whose answer is not known

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asks:
What is the law: does it become a handle for its fellow?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the neighbor's half of the corner stone, and 'its fellow' is the half in the house with the נגע.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי זֵירָא מַהוּ שֶׁתֵּעָשֶׂה יָד לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up on the corner-stone משנה quoted in step 6, in the same way רב פפא asked a handle question in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the rule of יד (handle) applies to a stone with a נגע, linking one half of the stone to the other.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא's question ends with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot settle רבי זירא's question, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the third handle-type question on this עמוד that ends with no answer. The גמרא found no source that decides whether a יד works for נגעי בתים.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question stays open with no answer

steps.whatToRemember: All three 'handle' questions in this section (the gourd, the fig branch, the shared stone) end with תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question asked in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no ruling on whether one half of a shared נגע stone is a handle for the other half.

steps.title: What is the difference between a limb from a living animal and a limb from a נבלה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's words 'the animal died' and asks what practical difference there is between אבר מן החי and אבר מן הנבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says, 'If the animal died.' What difference is there between a limb from a living animal and a limb from a נבלה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting the next words of the משנה, 'the animal died.' It then asks what difference it makes whether the hanging limb counts as a limb from a living animal or as a limb from a נבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that once the animal dies, the hanging limb is טמא as אבר מן החי but not as אבר מן הנבלה. Both kinds of limb make things טמא, so the גמרא wants to know why this difference matters at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb cut off from a living animal
An animal that died without proper שחיטה
What difference is there between; asks for the practical result of two categories

phrases.english: "If the animal died."

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי
phrases.english: What difference is there between a limb from a living animal
and a limb from a carcass?
phrases.notes: Some versions say שֶׁל, in the round brackets. The corrected wording is מִן, in the square brackets. The meaning is the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי לְאֵבֶר מִן הַנְּבֵלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the handle questions behind and returns to the next words of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between the טומאה of אבר מן החי and the טומאה of אבר מן הנבלה.

steps.title: The difference is flesh that separates from the limb
steps.stepSummary: Flesh that separates from a limb of a living animal is not טמא, but flesh that separates from a limb of a נבלה is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: flesh that separates from the limb. Flesh that separates from a limb of a living animal does not make things טמא. Flesh that separates from a limb of a נבלה does make things טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9. The difference shows up when a piece of flesh comes off the limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flesh that separates from a limb of a living animal is treated like flesh that comes straight off a living animal, so it is טהור. Flesh from a limb of a נבלה is treated like נבלה meat, so it is טמא. That is why the משנה needed to say that the hanging limb is only אבר מן החי.

keyTerms.meaning: Flesh that separates or comes off
Makes things טמא; passes on טומאה
There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: Both limbs are טמא, but only flesh coming off a נבלה's limb is טמא. Flesh coming off a living animal's limb is not.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think אבר מן החי is טהור. The whole limb is טמא. Only flesh that separates from it on its own is טהור.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
regarding flesh that separates from it (from an animal's limb),
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. Either way, 'it' here is the limb.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִילּוּ בָּשָׂר הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מֵאֵבֶר מִן הַחַי –
phrases.english: for flesh that separates from a limb of a living animal
does not make things impure,
but flesh from a limb of a carcass does make things impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is flesh that separates from the limb: it is טהור if the limb came from a living animal, and טמא if the limb came from a נבלה.

steps.title: What is the source that a limb from a living animal is טמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which פסוק teaches that אבר מן החי makes things טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A limb from a living animal makes things טמא. What is the verse for this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the source of a rule it has been assuming, that a limb taken from a living animal is טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual פסוקים about טומאה speak about an animal that died. A limb taken from an animal that is still alive is not obviously included, so the גמרא needs a פסוק that covers it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse? A request for the source in the תורה
That it makes things טמא
A verse from the תורה

phrases.english: That a limb from a living animal makes things impure,
what is the verse?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי דִּמְטַמֵּא מַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the difference between the two kinds of limb is explained, the גמרא asks for the source of the טומאה of אבר מן החי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches that אבר מן החי is טמא.

steps.title: The source is 'And if some of the animal dies'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, brings the פסוק 'וכי ימות מן הבהמה' as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: the verse is 'And if some of the animal dies.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה, in the name of רב, answers the question from step 11 with a פסוק from ויקרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said 'if an animal dies.' Instead it says 'מן הבהמה,' which can be read as 'part of the animal.' This reading includes a limb taken from an animal in the טומאה of נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it dies
From the animal; can be read as 'part of the animal'

steps.whyThisMatters: This פסוק is the תורה source for treating אבר מן החי as a source of טומאה, which the rest of this משנה depends on.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
"And if some of the animal dies."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:39. The word מִן, 'from' or 'part of,' hints that even a part of the animal, like a limb, is included.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב וְכִי יָמוּת מִן הַבְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is ויקרא 11:39, 'וכי ימות מן הבהמה.' The word 'מן' includes a part of the animal, so a limb taken from a living animal is טמא.

steps.title: The verse is already needed for a slaughtered טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: the פסוק 'וכי ימות מן הבהמה' is already used for a different law. That law is that a טרפה that was slaughtered does not make things טמא as a נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this verse is needed for another teaching of רב יהודה in the name of רב (some say it is a ברייתא): 'And if some of the animal dies' means that some animals make things טמא and some do not. Which one does not? A טרפה that was slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the source רב just gave. That same פסוק is already busy teaching a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מן' ('some of') limits the טומאה of נבלה, so that not every dead animal is included. That limit is used to exclude a טרפה that had שחיטה. If the פסוק is used up for that, how can רב also learn אבר מן החי from it?

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for something else. The verse is already used for another law.
Some or part. Here it is learned from the word 'מן'.
A fatally wounded animal that was slaughtered properly. It is still forbidden to eat, but it is not טמא as a נבלה.
Makes things טמא (ritually impure).

steps.confusionAlert: A slaughtered טרפה is still forbidden to eat. The פסוק only teaches that it does not make things טמא the way a נבלה does.

phrases.english: But this [verse] is needed
for the other [teaching] that רב יהודה said in the name of רב,
as רב יהודה said in the name of רב,
and some say it was taught in a ברייתא:
'And if some of the animal dies'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:39

phrases.english: some animals make things טמא,
and some animals do not make things טמא.
And which is this?
This is a טרפה that one slaughtered!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source רב gave in step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's use of 'וכי ימות מן הבהמה' as the source for אבר מן החי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is already used to exclude a slaughtered טרפה, so it cannot also teach אבר מן החי.

steps.title: The extra words teach two laws
steps.stepSummary: The תורה could have written the single word 'מבהמה'. Writing two words, 'מן הבהמה', shows that the פסוק teaches both laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the תורה should have written 'מבהמה'. Why does it say 'מן הבהמה'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The פסוק has extra wording, so it can teach both laws at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מבהמה' would have been enough to teach one law. The longer form 'מן הבהמה' adds wording, so we learn two things: a slaughtered טרפה is not טמא, and אבר מן החי is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳.
Learn two things from it.

phrases.english: If so, let the Merciful One write 'מבהמה' ('from an animal'),
What is [the point of] 'מן הבהמה'?
Learn two [things] from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording in the פסוק allows two teachings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק only has room for one law, the slaughtered טרפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra wording of 'מן הבהמה' teaches both the slaughtered טרפה and אבר מן החי.

steps.title: Then flesh should also be טמא
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק teaches that a part of a living animal is טמא, then flesh that separates from a living animal should also be טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, flesh too [should be טמא]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. If a limb from a living animal is טמא, why not a piece of flesh too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only speaks of 'מן הבהמה', a part of the animal. Plain flesh is also a part of the animal, so it seems it should be included as well.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, meaning if that is true.
Flesh or meat, without bone or sinew.

phrases.english: If so, even flesh too [should be טמא]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source now accepted in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation of אבר מן החי from 'מן הבהמה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same פסוק would seem to include flesh as well, which goes against step 10, where flesh from a living animal is not טמא.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: only what does not grow back
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא excludes flesh. Just as death cannot be replaced, only a part that does not grow back is טמא. Flesh grows back, so it is not טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not think so. As a ברייתא teaches: One might think flesh that separates from a living animal is טמא. So the פסוק says 'And if some of the animal dies'. Just as death does not make replacements, so too only something that does not make replacements. These are the words of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. Flesh is excluded because it grows back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי compares the separated part to death itself: what is lost cannot return. A cut-off limb never grows back, so it is like death and is טמא. Flesh heals and fills in again, so it is not טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not even think it.
The פסוק teaches.
Replacements, meaning something that grows back.
Death.

phrases.english: Do not think so,
as it was taught: One might think that flesh
that separates from a living [animal] is טמא?
The verse says: 'And if some of the animal dies'.
Just as death does not make replacements,
phrases.notes: Once something has died, it does not come back.

phrases.english: so too [only] anything that does not make replacements [is טמא],
phrases.notes: A limb does not grow back, but flesh does.

phrases.english: these are the words of רבי יוסי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: A ברייתא limits the פסוק using the comparison to death
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any part of a living animal, even flesh, is טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a part that does not grow back is טמא. Flesh grows back, so it is not טמא.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: like a whole animal, with sinews and bones
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns from the word 'בהמה'. A part is טמא only if, like a whole animal, it has sinews and bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: 'Animal'. Just as an animal has sinews and bones, so too anything with sinews and bones.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second reason why flesh is not טמא, this time in the name of רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not use the idea of growing back. He says the part must look like a small animal, with sinews and bones. Plain flesh has neither, so it is not טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Sinews.
Bones.

phrases.english: רבי עקיבא says: 'Animal'.
Just as an animal [has] sinews and bones,
so too anything [with] sinews and bones [is טמא].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second derivation in the ברייתא, different from רבי יוסי's
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A part from a living animal is טמא only if it has sinews and bones.

steps.title: רבי: like a whole animal, with flesh, sinews and bones
steps.stepSummary: רבי also learns from 'בהמה', but requires all three: flesh, sinews and bones, just like a whole animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: 'Animal'. Just as an animal has flesh, sinews and bones, so too anything with flesh, sinews and bones.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a third opinion, from רבי. It is like רבי עקיבא's, but adds flesh to the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, the part must have all three things a whole animal has: flesh, sinews and bones. That is what a limb is. Flesh alone is missing sinews and bones, so it is not טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: So too anything. This is the phrase that extends the comparison.

steps.whatToRemember: All three opinions agree on the outcome: a limb from a living animal is טמא, but flesh alone is not. They disagree only on the reason. רבי יוסי says it is because the limb does not grow back. רבי עקיבא says it is because the limb has sinews and bones. רבי says it is because the limb has flesh, sinews and bones.

phrases.english: רבי says: 'Animal'.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה הנשיא, who is usually just called 'רבי'.

phrases.english: Just as an animal [has] flesh, sinews and bones,
so too anything [with] flesh, sinews and bones [is טמא].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third derivation in the ברייתא, adding flesh to רבי עקיבא's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A part from a living animal is טמא only if it has flesh, sinews and bones.

steps.title: What is the difference between רבי and רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a practical case where רבי and רבי עקיבא would rule differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference between רבי and רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what real case would come out differently according to רבי and according to רבי עקיבא. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא needs sinews and bones. רבי needs flesh, sinews and bones. The two opinions sound very close, so the גמרא wants to find a case where the extra word 'flesh' actually changes the law.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between: asks for a case where two opinions give different results
Flesh, meat
Sinews
Bones

phrases.english: What is there
between רבי and רבי עקיבא?
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no other name means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the one who put together the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two opinions just quoted in steps 17 and 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where requiring flesh (רבי) changes the outcome compared with requiring only sinews and bones (רבי עקיבא).

steps.title: The difference is the knee joint
steps.stepSummary: The difference between them is the ארכובה, which has sinews and bones but no flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is the knee joint.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions differ about the ארכובה, the leg joint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארכובה has sinews and bones but no flesh. רבי עקיבא only needs sinews and bones, so for him it is טמא when it falls off a living animal. רבי needs flesh too, so for him it is not טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
Knee or leg joint, which has sinews and bones but no flesh
A limb from a living animal, the subject of this whole discussion

phrases.english: The difference between them is the knee joint.
phrases.notes: The joint has sinews and bones but no flesh, so only רבי עקיבא's test is met.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ארכובה: טמא for רבי עקיבא (it has sinews and bones), not טמא for רבי (it has no flesh).

steps.title: What is the difference between רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks for a practical case where רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי would disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Between רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי, what is the difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next pair of opinions and asks where they differ in practice. This sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי's test is whether the part grows back (חליפין). רבי עקיבא's test is whether the part has sinews and bones. These are two completely different tests, so the גמרא looks for a part that passes one test and fails the other.

keyTerms.meaning: A replacement: a part that grows back
Animal: the word רבי עקיבא learns his rule from

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי,
phrases.english: Between רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי,
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי הגלילי is the one behind the ברייתא in step 16: only a part that does not grow back is טמא.

phrases.english: what difference is there between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question as step 19, now about a different pair of opinions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where the 'does not grow back' test and the 'sinews and bones' test give different results.

steps.title: רב פפא: the kidney and the upper lip
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the difference is the kidney and the upper lip, which do not grow back but have no bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The kidney and the upper lip are the difference between them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי disagree about a kidney or an upper lip that separates from a living animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A kidney and an upper lip do not grow back, so for רבי יוסי הגלילי they are טמא. They have no bones, so for רבי עקיבא they are not טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Kidney
The upper lip

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
The kidney and the upper lip
are the difference between them.
phrases.notes: These parts never grow back, but they have no bone. So רבי יוסי הגלילי says טמא and רבי עקיבא says not טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כּוּלְיָא וְנִיב שְׂפָתַיִם אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Kidney and upper lip: טמא for רבי יוסי הגלילי (they do not grow back), not טמא for רבי עקיבא (no bones).
steps.whatToRemember: Three tests, three practical differences: grows back or not (רבי יוסי הגלילי); sinews and bones (רבי עקיבא); flesh, sinews and bones (רבי). Knee joint splits רבי from רבי עקיבא; kidney and upper lip split רבי עקיבא from רבי יוסי הגלילי.

steps.title: A parallel ברייתא about שרצים: רבי יוסי הגלילי's view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the same argument about a living שרץ. רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from 'במותם' that only a part that does not grow back is טמא, so flesh is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught about שרצים in the same way: You might think that flesh that separates from a שרץ is טמא. The פסוק says 'when they are dead': just as death does not have a replacement, so too only something that does not have a replacement is טמא. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that the same three תנאים argue in the same way about a שרץ, a small creeping creature. This step gives רבי יוסי הגלילי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the טומאה of שרצים uses the word 'במותם' (when they are dead). Death is final and cannot be replaced. So רבי יוסי הגלילי says a part of a living שרץ is טמא only if it also does not grow back, and flesh is excluded because it grows back.

keyTerms.meaning: Regarding, about
In the same way, like this case
Small creeping creatures whose dead bodies are טמא
You might have thought: brings up an idea the ברייתא will reject
The פסוק teaches: brings the פסוק that answers the 'you might think'
When they are dead

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי גַּבֵּי שְׁרָצִים כְּהַאי גַּוְונָא:
phrases.english: It is also taught about creeping creatures in the same way:
You might think that flesh that separates from creeping creatures
phrases.notes: This means while the שרץ is still alive.

phrases.english: should be impure?
So the verse says: 'when they are dead'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:32

phrases.english: just as death does not produce a replacement,
so too only anything that does not produce a replacement is impure.
These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי גַּבֵּי שְׁרָצִים כְּהַאי גַּוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the same three opinions about an animal also appear about a שרץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי הגלילי: from 'במותם', a part separating from a living שרץ is טמא only if it does not grow back; flesh is excluded.
steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא uses a different פסוק ('במותם', about שרצים) from the one about animals, but the logic is the same as step 16: death cannot be replaced, so the טמא part must be one that cannot be replaced.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא on שרצים: sinews and bones
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns from the word 'שרץ' that a part is טמא only if it has sinews and bones, like a whole שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: Learn it from 'שרץ'. Just as a שרץ has sinews and bones, so too any part with sinews and bones is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי עקיבא's view about שרצים, which matches his view about animals in step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not use the 'replacement' idea. He compares the part to a whole שרץ: a whole שרץ has sinews and bones, so a part is טמא only if it has sinews and bones too.

keyTerms.meaning: A single creeping creature
Just as ... so too: a comparison that sets the rule

phrases.english: רבי עקיבא says: Learn it from the word 'creeping creature':
just as a creeping creature has sinews and bones,
so too anything with sinews and bones is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source and test from רבי יוסי הגלילי's in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: a part of a living שרץ is טמא only if it has sinews and bones.

steps.title: רבי on שרצים: flesh, sinews and bones
steps.stepSummary: רבי also learns from 'שרץ', but requires flesh, sinews and bones, like a whole שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: Learn it from 'שרץ'. Just as a שרץ has flesh, sinews and bones, so too any part with flesh, sinews and bones is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with רבי's view about שרצים, which matches his view about animals in step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי uses the same word as רבי עקיבא but adds flesh to the list. So a part is טמא only if it is like a complete שרץ, with all three: flesh, sinews and bones.

keyTerms.meaning: So too anything: applies the comparison to every part

steps.whatToRemember: The three opinions about שרצים match the three about animals exactly: no replacement (רבי יוסי הגלילי), sinews and bones (רבי עקיבא), flesh, sinews and bones (רבי).

phrases.english: רבי says: Learn it from the word 'creeping creature':
just as a creeping creature has flesh, sinews and bones,
so too anything with flesh, sinews and bones is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same word as רבי עקיבא in step 24 but adds flesh to the requirement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: a part of a living שרץ is טמא only if it has flesh, sinews and bones.

steps.title: Where רבי and רבי עקיבא differ: the knee joint
steps.stepSummary: The difference between רבי and רבי עקיבא is a knee joint, which has sinews and bones but no flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Between רבי and רבי עקיבא, the difference is the knee joint.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a real case where רבי and רבי עקיבא, from the last two steps, reach different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא needs only sinews and bones for the part to be טמא. רבי needs flesh, sinews and bones. A knee joint has sinews and bones but no flesh, so it is טמא for רבי עקיבא and טהור for רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: The knee or leg joint. It has sinews and bones but no flesh.
'There is between them.' This phrase points to the practical difference between two opinions.
Sinews and bones.

phrases.english: Between Rabbi and Rabbi Akiva
the difference between them is the leg joint.
phrases.notes: A knee joint has sinews and bones but no flesh. That is exactly the point the two of them argue about.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין רַבִּי לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the two readings of 'שרץ' from steps 24-25 into a concrete case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A knee joint (sinews and bones, no flesh) is the case where רבי and רבי עקיבא disagree.

steps.title: Asking where רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי differ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the practical difference between רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי about a living שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Between רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי, what is the difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a real case where רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי would rule differently. This sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (steps 21-22) the same question was asked about a living בהמה. Now it is asked again for the שרץ ברייתא, so the גמרא repeats the question here on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What?' This opens a question.
One of the eight small creeping creatures whose dead body makes things טמא.
'When they are dead' (ויקרא 11:32). רבי יוסי הגלילי learns his rule from this word.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
phrases.english: Between Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yosei HaGelili
what is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רבי and רבי עקיבא difference, it asks about the other pair of opinions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete case where 'does not grow back' (רבי יוסי הגלילי) and 'sinews and bones' (רבי עקיבא) give different results.

steps.title: רב פפא: the kidney and the upper lip
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the difference is the kidney and the upper lip.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the difference between them is the kidney and the upper lip.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the case: a kidney or upper lip cut from a living שרץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These parts do not grow back, so for רבי יוסי הגלילי they are טמא. They have no bones, so for רבי עקיבא, who needs sinews and bones, they are טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Kidney.
The upper lip.

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on a part from a living שרץ: רבי יוסי הגלילי says it is טמא if it does not grow back. רבי עקיבא needs sinews and bones. רבי needs flesh, sinews and bones. The knee joint and the kidney or lip are the cases that separate them.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כּוּלְיָא וְנִיב שְׂפָתַיִם
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The kidney and the upper lip
are the difference between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Parts that do not grow back but have no bones, like the kidney and upper lip, are טמא for רבי יוסי הגלילי and טהור for רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Why the בהמה case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The rule had to be taught for a שרץ too. A שרץ makes things טמא even in a lentil-size piece, so we might have thought a piece from a living שרץ is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both cases are needed. If we were only taught about a בהמה, we would say a piece from a living בהמה is not טמא because a dead בהמה does not make things טמא in a lentil-size piece. But a שרץ does make things טמא in a lentil-size piece, so we might say a piece from a living שרץ is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the rule about pieces cut from a living animal had to be taught for both a בהמה and a שרץ. Here it shows why the בהמה case alone would not teach us about a שרץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead בהמה only makes things טמא in an olive-size piece (כזית), but a dead שרץ does so even in a lentil-size piece (כעדשה). Because a שרץ's טומאה is stronger in this way, we might have thought even a piece from a living one is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it is necessary.' The גמרא is showing that two teachings that look alike are both needed.
'Taught us.'
'This is the reason.'
The size of a lentil. This is the smallest amount of a dead שרץ that makes things טמא.
From a living creature.
'I would say.' This is what we might have wrongly thought.

phrases.english: And it is necessary, for if it had taught us only about an animal –
this is the reason it does not make impure from the living:
because it does not make impure in a lentil-bulk,
phrases.notes: A dead בהמה needs at least an olive-size piece to make things טמא.

phrases.english: but a creeping animal, which makes impure in a lentil-bulk –
I would say it makes impure from the living.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the details of the argument to why both the בהמה and the שרץ teachings are needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without the שרץ teaching, its lentil-size טומאה might have made us think a piece from a living שרץ is טמא.

steps.title: Why the שרץ case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The rule also had to be taught for a בהמה. A dead בהמה makes things טמא by carrying, so we might have thought a piece from a living בהמה is טמא. So both are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we were only taught about a שרץ, we would say a piece from it is not טמא because a שרץ does not make things טמא by carrying. But a בהמה does make things טמא by carrying, so we might say a piece from a living בהמה is טמא. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the 'both are needed' argument from the other side and ends: צריכא, both teachings are necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the בהמה has the stronger טומאה: a dead בהמה makes a person who carries it טמא (טומאת משא), but a dead שרץ does not. Each creature is stronger in one way, so neither case could be learned from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying. A dead בהמה makes the person carrying it טמא, even without touching it.
A domesticated animal, like a cow or sheep.
'It should make impure.'

steps.whatToRemember: A שרץ is stronger in size (a lentil-size piece is enough). A בהמה is stronger in carrying (משא). So the rule that a piece from a living creature is not טמא had to be taught for both.
steps.confusionAlert: צריכא does not mean the two cases have different rules. Both rules are the same. The גמרא is only explaining why we could not learn one case from the other.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only about a creeping animal,
because it does not make impure by carrying –
it does not make impure from the living,
but an animal, which makes impure by carrying –
I would say it should make impure from the living; therefore it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other half of the צריכא argument and ends it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both teachings are needed. Each creature has a stronger side (the lentil size for a שרץ, carrying for a בהמה) that could have made us think a piece from the living one is טמא.

steps.title: New ברייתא: flesh cut from an אבר מן החי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says: if someone cuts an olive-size piece of flesh from a limb taken from a living animal, and only after cutting decides to use it as food, it is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Someone cuts an olive-size piece of flesh from a limb taken from a living animal. If he cut it off and only afterwards decided to use it as food, it is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא, still about flesh from a living animal. This opens a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flesh from an אבר מן החי does not carry the טומאה of a dead body (נבלה). It can only become טמא as food after the owner decides to use it as food. Here he decided only after cutting it off, when it was no longer touching the limb, so it stays טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: One who cuts.
The size of an olive. This is the basic amount for many laws.
A limb taken from a living animal.
He intended or decided. Here it means he decided to use the flesh as food.
Pure; not טמא.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: One who cuts an olive-bulk of flesh
from a limb from the living animal,

phrases.aramaic: חֲתָכוֹ וְאַחַר כָּךְ חִישֵּׁב עָלָיו – טָהוֹר.
phrases.english: if he cut it and afterward intended it for food – it is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַחוֹתֵךְ כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר מֵאֵבֶר מִן הַחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about flesh from a living animal, after the צריכא discussion is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flesh cut from an אבר מן החי and only then set aside for food is טהור.

steps.title: Deciding first, then cutting: the flesh is impure
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the ברייתא says that if a person decided to use the flesh as food while it was still attached to the limb, and only then cut it off, it is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he planned to use it as food and only afterward cut it off, it is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ברייתא from step 31 with the opposite order of events: first the decision to use it as food, then the cutting. Here the flesh is טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become טמא once it counts as food, and a person's decision (מחשבה) is what makes this flesh count as food. In step 31 the decision came after cutting, so the flesh was never food while touching the limb, and it stayed טהור. Here the decision came first, so it was already food while attached to the אבר מן החי, which is a source of טומאה, and it is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought about it, meaning he decided to use it as food
Ritually impure
A limb taken from a living animal, which is a source of טומאה
A person's intention or decision, which can make something count as food

steps.whatToRemember: Order matters. If he cut first and decided later, it is טהור. If he decided first and cut later, it is טמא.

phrases.english: If he planned to use it as food,
phrases.notes: This is still the same piece of flesh from step 31. Since a Jew may not eat it, he means using it as food for a non-Jew.

phrases.english: and afterward he cut it off, it is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: חִישֵּׁב עָלָיו, וְאַחַר כָּךְ חֲתָכוֹ – טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא started in step 31 by giving the opposite case (decision before cutting).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flesh that was set aside as food while still attached to an אבר מן החי, and then cut off, is טמא.

steps.title: רבי אסי asks what was said in the study hall
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי missed the בית מדרש and asks רבי זירא what was taught there. רבי זירא answers with his own question: what is bothering you?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי did not go to the study hall. He met רבי זירא and asked him: What was said in the study hall? רבי זירא said to him: What is difficult for you?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a short story that leads into a question on the ברייתא. It sets up the next move: רבי אסי is about to say what is troubling him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי wants to know what was discussed that day. רבי זירא does not give a summary. He asks which point is bothering רבי אסי, so the talk can focus on that issue.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall where the חכמים learned together
Did not go in
What is difficult for you?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַסִּי לָא עָל לְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi did not go into the study hall,
he found Rabbi Zeira,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי אֲמוּר בְּבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא?
phrases.english: he said to him: What was said in the study hall?
He said to him: What is difficult for you?
phrases.notes: Now רבי זירא is the one speaking. He wants to know which point רבי אסי is stuck on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a story that will question the ruling just stated in step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was taught in the בית מדרש, and which point is troubling רבי אסי.

steps.title: רבי אסי points to the ruling that troubles him
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי says his difficulty is the ברייתא's ruling that if he decided first and then cut, the flesh is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is taught, that if he planned to use it as food and afterward cut it off, it is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי names the exact ruling that bothers him, which is the case from step 32. This is a setup line: the reason it is hard comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא quotes the ruling of the ברייתא again on purpose. This time it is not teaching the law but marking it as the target of a question. What exactly is hard about it is spelled out in the continuation of the conversation on the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה
He cut it off

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ruling. It is the same ruling from step 32, repeated because רבי אסי is about to question it.

phrases.english: He said to him: That which is taught:
If he planned it as food and afterward cut it off, it is impure.
phrases.notes: This is the ruling from step 32, quoted again because it is what bothers רבי אסי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, דְּקָתָנֵי: חִישֵּׁב וְאַחַר כָּךְ חֲתָכוֹ טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question by naming the troubling ruling from step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that flesh set aside as food before being cut from an אבר מן החי is טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Set up only here. רבי אסי marks the ruling as hard to understand, and the reason is given in the next part of the גמרא.
